topic.name: The Change of Base Formula for Logarithms

question.text: Use a calculator to evaluate $\log_{12} (23) $ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
Let's calculate $\log_{12} (23)$ by changing the base $12$ to the common logarithm (base $10$).

We use the change of base formula: \[ \log_a X = \dfrac {\log_b X} {\log_b a} \]

In our case, $a=12,$ $X =23,$ $b=10.$ So, we have

\begin{align*} \log_{12} (23) & = \dfrac {\log_{10} (23)} {\log_{10} (12)} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {\log (23)} {\log (12)} \\[5pt] & \approx \dfrac{1.361\,728}{1.079\,181}\\[5pt] & \approx 1.262 \end{align*}

example.title: Evaluating a Logarithm With a Calculator Using the Change of Base Formula

question.explanation:
We use the change of base formula:

\[ \log_a X = \dfrac {\log_b X} {\log_b a} \]

In our case, $a=64$ and $X = \sqrt{8}.$ Since both $a$ and $X$ can be presented as a power of $8,$ we set $b=8.$ So, we have:

\begin{align*} \log_{64}\left(\sqrt{8}\right)&=\dfrac {\log_{8}\left(\sqrt{8}\right)} {\log_{8}(64)} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac {\log_{8}\left(8^{1/2}\right)} {\log_{8}\left(8^{2}\right)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} {2} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1} {4} \end{align*}

example.title: Evaluating a Logarithm Without a Calculator Using the Change of Base Formula

question.explanation:
We use the change of base formula:

\[ \log_a X = \dfrac {\log_b X} {\log_b a} \]

In our case, $a=64$ and $X = \sqrt[3]{4}.$ Since both $a$ and $X$ can be presented as a power of $4,$ we set $b=4.$ So, we have:

\begin{align*} \log_{64}\left(\sqrt[3]{4}\right)&=\dfrac {\log_{4}\left(\sqrt[3]{4}\right)} {\log_{4}(64)} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac {\log_{4}\left(4^{1/3}\right)} {\log_{4}\left(4^{3}\right)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)} {3} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1} {9} \end{align*}
